questions.title: How does the blockwise local softmax in FlashAttention-3 yield the exact global softmax output?
questions.question_body:
In the forward algorithm, each CTA processes a query tile $\mathbf{Q}_i$ and loops over key-value blocks $\{(\mathbf{K}_j, \mathbf{V}_j)\}$. The kernel keeps per-row running statistics $m_i$ and $\ell_i$ and updates them via
- $m_i \leftarrow \max\big(m_i, \operatorname{rowmax}(\mathbf{S}_i^{(j)})\big)$ where $\mathbf{S}_i^{(j)} = \mathbf{Q}_i \mathbf{K}_j^\top$,
- $\widetilde{\mathbf{P}}_i^{(j)} = \exp(\mathbf{S}_i^{(j)} - m_i)$,
- $\ell_i \leftarrow e^{m_i^{\text{old}} - m_i}\,\ell_i + \operatorname{rowsum}(\widetilde{\mathbf{P}}_i^{(j)})$,
- $\mathbf{O}_i \leftarrow e^{-(m_i - m_i^{\text{old}})}\,\mathbf{O}_i + \widetilde{\mathbf{P}}_i^{(j)} \mathbf{V}_j$,
and finally returns $\mathbf{O}_i \leftarrow \operatorname{diag}(\ell_i)^{-1} \mathbf{O}_i$.
Could someone provide a concise derivation that the final $\mathbf{O}_i$ equals $\operatorname{softmax}(\alpha\mathbf{Q}_i \mathbf{K}^\top)\,\mathbf{V}$ computed exactly (no approximation), and explain why the multiplicative rescalings with $m_i$ and $\ell_i$ preserve numerical stability and correctness?

questions.title: What exactly are commit-but-don’t-wait semantics for WGMMA and TMA in the 2-stage pipeline?
questions.question_body: The 2-stage consumer pseudocode issues WGMMA for $\mathbf{Q}_i\mathbf{K}_j^\top$ and for $\widetilde{\mathbf{P}}_{\mathrm{cur}}\mathbf{V}_{j-1}$ with commit but do not wait, then waits later before using the results. What are the concrete PTX or CUTLASS primitives that implement these semantics for Hopper (e.g., wgmma.mma_async and the corresponding wait)? Similarly, what are the TMA primitives and barriers used to signal tile readiness from producer to consumer? How do these primitives guarantee that softmax never reads $\mathbf{S}_{\mathrm{next}}$ until its GEMM has completed, even under aggressive compiler instruction reordering?

questions.title: How does pingpong scheduling actually overlap softmax with GEMMs across warpgroups?
questions.question_body: The paper says bar.sync is used to force GEMMs in warpgroup 1 before GEMMs in warpgroup 2, so that softmax in one warpgroup runs while Tensor Cores are busy in the other. How is this ordering sufficient to induce concurrent MFU (for exp) and Tensor Core usage on Hopper’s scheduler? Is there a minimal number of consumer warps per warpgroup needed for this to be effective, and what ensures the softmax instructions are not delayed until after the GEMMs complete anyway?

questions.title: How are the circular SMEM buffer stages synchronized to avoid races between producer and consumers?
questions.question_body: The forward pass uses an s-stage circular buffer in SMEM for $\{\mathbf{K}_j,\mathbf{V}_j\}$ and mentions a pipeline object that manages synchronization. What specific barrier primitives are used (e.g., mbarrier, bar.sync, or CUTLASS pipeline abstractions) to implement: (1) producer waiting for a stage to be consumed, (2) producer committing a stage as ready, (3) consumers releasing stages back to the producer? Are $\mathbf{K}$ and $\mathbf{V}$ staged separately or as a pair sharing the same stage index, and how do you prevent the consumer from reading a $\mathbf{V}_j$ tile whose in-kernel transpose has not completed yet?

questions.title: What are SS-GEMM and RS-GEMM in the pseudocode, and why are they different?
questions.question_body: The consumer loop refers to SS-GEMM for $\mathbf{Q}_i \mathbf{K}_j^\top$ and RS-GEMM for $\widetilde{\mathbf{P}}_i^{(j)} \mathbf{V}_j$. What exactly does SS versus RS denote here (e.g., which operand is sourced from SMEM versus registers), and how does that map to Hopper’s WGMMA operand modes? Why is this asymmetry useful or necessary in FA-3 compared to a symmetric SMEM-sourced GEMM on both operands?

questions.title: How is causal masking integrated into the overlapped 2-stage pipeline without breaking the softmax rescaling invariants?
questions.question_body: For causal attention, only entries with key position $\le$ query position are valid. In the FA-3 2-stage main loop, softmax of iteration $j+1$ overlaps with the second GEMM of iteration $j$. How are masked columns handled when updating $m_i$, $\ell_i$, and $\mathbf{O}_i$ at tile boundaries, especially when a query block $\mathbf{Q}_i$ spans multiple causal blocks? Do you zero out masked parts of $\mathbf{S}_i^{(j)}$ before the rowmax and rowsum updates, or apply an additive $-\infty$ mask inside the log-sum-exp update? Any special care needed at the first valid $\mathbf{K}_j$ for a given $\mathbf{Q}_i$?

questions.title: Why is forward FLOPs estimated as $4\,N^2 d\,H$ and backward as about $2.5\times$ forward?
questions.question_body: The benchmarking section uses forward FLOPs $= 4\cdot \text{seqlen}^2\cdot \text{head dimension}\cdot \text{number of heads}$, halved under causal masking, and backward FLOPs $\approx 2.5\times$ forward. Could someone derive the factor 4 for the two forward GEMMs and explain where the extra factors come from? For backward, there are 5 GEMMs due to recomputation; can you break down which shapes contribute and why the ratio is about $2.5$ instead of exactly $2.5$ or another value given softmax and rescaling overheads?

questions.title: For FP8 WGMMA, why must operands be k-major and how do LDSM/STSM enable an efficient in-kernel transpose of $\mathbf{V}$?
questions.question_body: The paper notes that FP8 WGMMA on Hopper only accepts k-major operands from SMEM, but typical $\mathbf{V}$ is stored contiguous in the head dimension (mn-major). They opt for an in-kernel transpose using LDSM and STSM. Could you explain concretely how a warp uses LDSM/STSM to read a tile of FP8 $\mathbf{V}$, transpose it, and store it back in SMEM in k-major form, including how FP8 values are packed into 16-bit lanes for these instructions and what extra register moves are required because transpose variants cannot split packed 8-bit pairs?

questions.title: How does permuting FP8 accumulator layout and matching the $\mathbf{V}$ tile permutation preserve correctness of $\mathbf{P}\mathbf{V}$?
questions.question_body: To bridge the layout mismatch between an FP8 WGMMA accumulator and the next FP8 operand layout, FA-3 applies a byte-permute to the FP32 accumulator so that the logical $\mathbf{P}$ tile’s columns are permuted by some permutation $\Pi$. The in-kernel $\mathbf{V}$ transpose then applies the matching row permutation $\Pi$ to $\mathbf{V}$. Is the claim that $(\mathbf{P}\Pi)(\Pi^{-1}\mathbf{V}) = \mathbf{P}\mathbf{V}$, and since you use the same $\Pi$ to permute $\mathbf{V}$’s rows, the product is unchanged? Could you show this explicitly for a tile, and clarify how you ensure the permutation is consistent across warps and iterations so that partial sums of $\mathbf{O}_i$ accumulate in the correct order?

questions.title: How are per-block FP8 scales folded into the computation at no extra cost?
questions.question_body: With block quantization, each $\mathbf{Q}$ block of shape $B_r\times d$ has its scale $s_Q$ and each $\mathbf{K}$ block of shape $B_c\times d$ has its scale $s_K$. One can write $\mathbf{Q}_{\text{fp}} \approx s_Q\,\mathbf{Q}_8$ and $\mathbf{K}_{\text{fp}} \approx s_K\,\mathbf{K}_8$. Then $\mathbf{S}_i^{(j)} = \mathbf{Q}_i\mathbf{K}_j^\top \approx (s_Q s_K)\, (\mathbf{Q}_{8,i}\mathbf{K}_{8,j}^\top)$. How exactly is the factor $s_Q s_K$ incorporated into the row-wise softmax with the running $m_i$ and $\ell_i$ without introducing extra flops? Do you fold it as an additive shift via $\log s_Q + \log s_K$ inside log-sum-exp, or multiply the partial probabilities before the second GEMM? A short, explicit formula for the updates would be very helpful.

questions.title: Why does the orthogonal incoherent transform preserve attention, and how is it fused with rotary embeddings?
questions.question_body: The paper multiplies $\mathbf{Q}$ and $\mathbf{K}$ by the same random orthogonal matrix $\mathbf{M}$ (Hadamard with random signs) before FP8 quantization to spread out outliers, relying on $(\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{M})(\mathbf{K}\mathbf{M})^\top = \mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^\top$. Do we need to use the same $\mathbf{M}$ across all heads and tokens, or can $\mathbf{M}$ vary per head? How is this fused with rotary embeddings, which apply position-dependent rotations in the head dimension? Does $\mathbf{M}$ commute with RoPE so that we can apply them in either order without changing $\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^\top$, and what is the precise $O(d\log d)$ algorithmic path used in-kernel?

questions.title: What exactly is the FP8 baseline for error, and how is RMSE computed fairly?
questions.question_body: The error experiment draws $\mathbf{Q},\mathbf{K},\mathbf{V}$ from a mixture that injects 0.1 percent outliers and compares RMSE against an FP64 reference. For the FP8 baseline, you state per-tensor scaling, FP32 accumulators, and softmax intermediates in FP16. Could you detail: (1) which operations are in FP8 vs FP16 vs FP32 for the baseline; (2) whether scales are chosen per input tensor or per matmul operand; (3) whether RMSE is measured on the final $\mathbf{O}$ after all rescalings; and (4) how seeds and sample sizes are controlled so the 2.6$\times$ improvement is statistically robust?

questions.title: Can you justify the 50 percent cycle estimate for exponentials in FP16 attention on H100?
questions.question_body: The text claims that for head dimension $d=128$ in FP16, there are about $512\times$ more matmul FLOPs than exponentials, but exponentials have $256\times$ lower throughput on H100, so the exponential can take about 50 percent of the time compared to matmul. Could you show a back-of-the-envelope calculation that relates: (a) the counts of exp operations per tile or per token pair, (b) GEMM FLOPs for $\mathbf{Q}\mathbf{K}^\top$ and $\mathbf{P}\mathbf{V}$, and (c) the hardware throughputs (989 TFLOPs for FP16 matmul vs roughly 3.9 TFLOPs-equivalent for special functions), to arrive at the 50 percent number?

questions.title: How should one pick tile sizes $B_r$, $B_c$ and the number of SMEM stages $s$ in practice?
questions.question_body: There are multiple trade-offs: larger tiles improve arithmetic intensity but increase register and SMEM pressure; the 2-stage pipeline requires extra registers to hold $\mathbf{S}_{\mathrm{next}}$; the in-kernel transpose of $\mathbf{V}$ may prefer particular $B_c$ multiples and alignments; and $s$ affects TMA overlap and SMEM footprint. Are there recommended heuristics for choosing $B_r$, $B_c$, and $s$ on H100 for common head dimensions (64, 128, 256), and how do these choices change between FP16 and FP8 kernels?

questions.title: How does setmaxnreg-based dynamic register reallocation interact with warp specialization?
questions.question_body: FA-3 uses setmaxnreg so producer warps (mostly issuing TMA and LDSM/STSM) give up registers to consumer warps (running WGMMAs and softmax). Is setmaxnreg applied per warpgroup or per warp, and is it static at kernel entry or can it change mid-kernel? How do you determine the target register counts to avoid spilling in the 2-stage pipeline while keeping enough occupancy, and are there hazards if a producer warp temporarily needs more registers for in-kernel $\mathbf{V}$ transposes?

questions.title: How are MQA and GQA supported without duplicating $\mathbf{K}$ and $\mathbf{V}$ in HBM?
questions.question_body: The paper says it follows the FA-2 approach for multi-query and grouped-query attention by adjusting indexing to avoid duplicating $\mathbf{K}$ and $\mathbf{V}$. Could you detail how the TMA loads and SMEM staging are organized so that multiple query heads reuse the same $\mathbf{K}_j, \mathbf{V}_j$ tiles, and how the consumer warps iterate over heads while keeping the producer-consumer ring buffer efficient?

questions.title: Which tensors use FP8, FP16, or FP32 in FP8 FlashAttention-3, and why?
questions.question_body: For the FP8 kernel, my understanding is: $\mathbf{Q},\mathbf{K},\mathbf{V}$ tiles are quantized to FP8 with per-block scales; both GEMMs run on FP8 Tensor Cores with FP32 accumulators; softmax intermediates ($m_i$, $\ell_i$, and $\widetilde{\mathbf{P}}$ before the second GEMM) are in FP32; and $\mathbf{O}_i$ is accumulated in FP32 before writing out. Is this accurate? If so, could you summarize the datatype of each buffer and intermediate and the points where dequantization or rescaling happens, and explain the rationale behind each precision choice?

questions.title: What is meant by a persistent kernel here, and why does lacking it hurt FP8 for small sequences and causal masks?
questions.question_body: The discussion mentions that FA-3 FP16 has a persistent kernel and load balancing strategy, while the FP8 version does not, contributing to worse performance at small sequence lengths and with causal masks relative to cuDNN. Can you define the persistent-kernel strategy you use (e.g., mapping CTAs persistently to SMs and looping over work tiles), how it interacts with warp specialization and the ring buffer, and why its absence particularly penalizes small or triangular workloads?

questions.title: What TMA alignment and shape constraints influence $B_c$ and SMEM layout for $\mathbf{K}$ and $\mathbf{V}$ tiles?
questions.question_body: On Hopper, TMA copies have preferred alignment and granularity (e.g., 128-byte alignment). When choosing $B_c$ and laying out SMEM tiles for $\mathbf{K}_j$ and $\mathbf{V}_j$, what constraints do you enforce to get peak bandwidth and avoid bank conflicts, especially when you plan to immediately apply LDSM/STSM to $\mathbf{V}_j$ for an in-kernel transpose? Any concrete guidelines on strides, leading dimensions, and padding that proved important in FA-3?
